decision: Keep G2 as one admitted-generation composition layer
why: The public contract is one project and one output scope; CLI, framework, validation policy, and release work are already separate Beads
evidence: genes-5x9c.2 acceptance criteria; development-session/v1/README.md; live tooling/AGENTS.md
result: Implement only createGenesDevelopmentSession and its internal adapters

decision: Reuse the compiler-owned v2 manifest as the candidate inventory
why: It is the only exact authority for generated-file ownership and stale deletion; scanning extensions or generated text would guess
result: Add one shared tooling manifest reader and build outer publication transitions from exact owned paths

decision: Keep host validation before public mutation and use the artifact callback only to verify an admission ticket
why: The artifact callback runs after physical moves, so expensive validation there would expose rejected bytes temporarily
result: Validate the private tree first; bind policy, output identity, and manifest digest into authorizationDigest

decision: Use a separate session generation marker as the outer transaction commit marker
why: An unchanged candidate must still advance generation, while the Genes ownership manifest can remain byte-identical
evidence: development-session vector unchanged-candidate-advances-generation; artifact plan requires a changed commit marker
result: Stage one private generation record and publish it last through the existing artifact transaction

why: The public v1 API intentionally asks only for project identity, invocation resolution, validation, and lifecycle controls
result: Export createGenesDevelopmentSession only; inject controlled primitives from an internal factory for exact conformance tests

decision: Report the generation acquired after a publication wait
why: A queued read begins after the writer commits and must identify the bytes it can actually read, not the generation current before it waited
evidence: writer-priority read fixture with a held second publication
result: Read the accepted generation only after acquiring the read side of the gate

decision: Reject public-output drift using the outer accepted marker
why: The compiler manifest names ownership but does not contain the previously admitted file digests; rereading edited output as prior state would silently bless manual changes
result: Persist the admitted manifest digest in the marker and compare it before every later publication

decision: Probe Haxe server readiness without using the first compilation as the probe
why: A real project compilation can legitimately exceed a short server-readiness deadline; readiness and build duration are different contracts
evidence: native TCP readiness plus real Haxe cold/warm integration
result: Use the loopback listener probe for readiness, then run every compilation through the normal connected/direct path

decision: Key the lifetime writer lock by project output rather than state directory
why: Two hosts can choose different private state directories while targeting the same public generated tree; state-local locks would not meet the one-writer contract
result: Store the lock at one deterministic project-relative path derived from the public output identity

decision: Mirror the compiler's UTF-16 manifest-scope spelling exactly
why: Haxe iterates a String by UTF-16 code unit while JavaScript for-of iterates Unicode code points; a non-BMP output filename would otherwise make tooling look for the wrong manifest
result: Iterate ownerIdentity with charCodeAt and preserve the compiler's two-underscore surrogate-pair spelling
